facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, subscription-based CTV platforms now offer starting tiers around $50.
facts.quote: Subscription-based platforms now offer starting tiers around $50, with the most common small-business CTV test budget falling in the $800-$2,500/month range.

facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, the most common small-business CTV test budget falls in the $800-$2,500 per month range.
facts.quote: with the most common small-business CTV test budget falling in the $800-$2,500/month range.

facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, a $50-$500 per month CTV budget is useful for very tight local geographies such as a 3-5 mile radius around a single location, but will not produce meaningful local frequency on its own.
facts.quote: Useful for very tight local geographies (a 3-5 mile radius around a single location)

facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, a $800-$1,500 per month CTV budget can build meaningful frequency of 3-5 impressions per household in a 5-12 mile service area over a 30-day window.
facts.quote: Enough to build meaningful frequency (3-5 impressions per household) in a 5-12 mile service area over a 30-day window.

facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, a $1,500-$2,500 per month CTV test budget produces a clean read at the 60-90 day mark.
facts.quote: Strong test budget that produces clean read at the 60-90 day mark.

facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, a $2,500-$5,000 per month CTV budget is the tier where most small businesses settle once a test has proven out.
facts.quote: No longer "small budget" territory, but worth noting as the tier where most small businesses settle in once a test has proven out.

facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, a $1,500 per month test run for 75 days commits $3,750 total to the test.
facts.quote: A $1,500/month test for 75 days commits $3,750 to the test.

facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, a CTV test should capture a minimum of four weeks of pre-launch baseline data, with six weeks being better.
facts.quote: Four weeks of pre-launch data is the minimum. Six weeks is better.

facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, the CTV platform needs the first 2 weeks of a campaign to settle into the area and find inventory, so optimization should wait.
facts.quote: The platform needs the first 2 weeks to settle into your area and find inventory.

facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, if more than 20-25% of CTV impressions land outside the real service area in the first read at week 7, the advertiser should contact platform support to tighten targeting.
facts.quote: If more than 20-25% of impressions are landing outside your real service area, contact CTV platform support to tighten targeting.

facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, a total conversion lift under 5% over baseline does not read as a win, while lift over 15% reads as a clear win.
facts.quote: If by less than 5%, the test isn't reading as a win. If by more than 15%, the test is reading as a clear win.

facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, a successful CTV test should be scaled with budget increases of 25-50% over the first 6 months.
facts.quote: consider modest budget increases (25-50% over the first 6 months)

facts.fact: Per the Adwave guide, the TV-running phase of a 90-day CTV test lasts 8 weeks (60 days) alongside the existing digital plan.
facts.quote: For 8 weeks (60 days), run TV alongside your existing digital plan.

facts.fact: Adwave advises launching a CTV test with at least two creatives.
facts.quote: launch with two creatives at minimum.

facts.fact: Adwave states that CTV needs 2-3 weeks to settle and another 4-6 weeks to demonstrate its lift on the broader funnel.
facts.quote: CTV needs 2-3 weeks to settle and another 4-6 weeks to demonstrate its lift on the broader funnel.

facts.fact: Adwave advises committing to 60-90 days before judging a CTV test.
facts.quote: commit to 60-90 days before judging.

facts.fact: Adwave claims that counting only TV-attributed conversions captures 30-50% of TV's real impact.
facts.quote: you'll capture 30-50% of TV's real impact.

facts.fact: Adwave states that a platform subscription for a small-budget CTV test costs $50-$500 of the monthly budget, depending on platform tier.
facts.quote: ($50-$500 of your monthly budget depending on platform tier)

facts.fact: Adwave cites a traditional TV production cost of $3,000-$8,000 for custom creative.
facts.quote: Save the $3,000-$8,000 traditional production cost for later

facts.fact: Adwave states that agency fees of $1,500-$3,500 per month would more than double the cost of a small-budget CTV test.
facts.quote: Agency fees of $1,500-$3,500/month would more than double your test cost

facts.fact: Adwave says most small business CTV tests at $1,000-$2,500 per month can be self-served.
facts.quote: Most small business CTV tests at $1,000-$2,500/month can be self-served.

facts.fact: Adwave's worked example of a plumbing company used a TV budget of $1,500 per month for 90 days, a total commitment of $4,500.
facts.quote: TV budget: $1,500/month for 90 days (total commitment: $4,500)

facts.fact: In Adwave's worked example, the plumbing company's existing digital spend was $1,800 per month on Meta plus $1,200 per month on Google, totaling $3,000 per month.
facts.quote: Existing $1,800/month Meta + $1,200/month Google = $3,000/month digital spend.

facts.fact: In Adwave's worked example, the plumbing company's average customer lifetime value was $1,800.
facts.quote: At the company's average customer lifetime value of $1,800

facts.fact: In Adwave's worked example, the company's average weekly inquiries rose from 38 at baseline to 47 during weeks 5-12, a reported increase of 24%.
facts.quote: Average weekly inquiries: 47 (+24% over baseline)

facts.fact: Adwave's worked example reports roughly 72 incremental inquiries during the 8-week TV window.
facts.quote: Incremental inquiries during the 8-week TV window: roughly 72 (9 per week × 8 weeks).

facts.fact: Adwave's worked example calculates $129,600 in additional lifetime customer value attributable to the campaign window.
facts.quote: that's $129,600 in additional lifetime customer value attributable to the campaign window.

facts.fact: Adwave's worked example reports a lifetime ROAS of roughly 43x on the TV spend.
facts.quote: lifetime ROAS works out to roughly 43x.

facts.fact: Adwave's worked example decided to scale TV spend from $1,500 to $2,200 per month.
facts.quote: scale TV from $1,500 to $2,200/month

facts.fact: Adwave advises against running CTV if monthly digital spend is under $1,000.
facts.quote: Your monthly digital spend is under $1,000.

facts.fact: Adwave says CTV works best when there is at least a 5-mile radius in which to build frequency.
facts.quote: CTV works best when there's at least a 5-mile radius in which to build frequency.

facts.fact: Adwave estimates most local small businesses need at least $800-$1,200 per month to build meaningful local frequency of 3-5 impressions per household.
facts.quote: Most local small businesses need at least $800-$1,200/month to build meaningful local frequency (3-5 impressions per household)

facts.fact: Adwave says a first CTV test should run 90 days minimum, made up of a 4-week baseline, an 8-week campaign, and a 1-week read.
facts.quote: 90 days minimum (with 4-week baseline + 8-week campaign + 1-week read).

facts.fact: Adwave says a campaign window shorter than 60 campaign days produces noisy data.
facts.quote: Going shorter than 60 campaign days produces noisy data

facts.fact: The page states that a small business is ready to test TV advertising if its monthly digital spend is at least $1,500-$2,000.
facts.quote: If your monthly digital spend is at least $1,500-$2,000, your website converts at acceptable rates, and you can sustain a $1,000-$2,500/month commitment for 90 days, you're ready to test.

facts.fact: The page states that a small business should be able to sustain a TV test commitment of $1,000-$2,500 per month for 90 days.
facts.quote: you can sustain a $1,000-$2,500/month commitment for 90 days, you're ready to test.
